title: The Man Who Built the Shelby Cobra
description:
He was told he had less than five years to live. So he quit racing, and built cars. Carroll Shelby had a heart defect from childhood, took nitroglycerin pills during races, and lived to eighty-nine. In between, he put an American engine in a British chassis, helped Ford win Le Mans, and had a heart transplant while working on the Dodge Viper. This is the story of the man who built the Shelby Cobra. Here is the twist. Before any of that, he was a chicken farmer whose farm went bankrupt. And the sources we read disagree on when he won Le Mans, on how he got the engine, and even on how many cars he made. We will tell his story as the sources do, and say where they conflict.

Every figure in this video comes from a published source, listed below.
